events.summary: President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that Fed Chair Jerome Powell ("Too Late") "should resign immediately", sharing an article about FHFA director William Pulte urging Congress to investigate Powell.
events.source_title: Trump says Fed Chair Jerome Powell 'should resign immediately' (Anadolu Agency, 3 Jul 2025)

events.summary: After media reports that Trump was likely to fire Powell, Trump said it was "highly unlikely unless he has to leave for fraud", referring to cost overruns in the $2.5bn renovation of Fed headquarters.
events.source_title: Trump repudiates draft letter to fire US Fed chair Powell (Al Jazeera, 16 Jul 2025)

events.summary: Trump announced he had fired Fed Governor Lisa Cook "for cause" over mortgage fraud allegations; Cook said no cause exists and sued on 28 Aug 2025. The D.C. Circuit (15 Sep 2025) and the Supreme Court (1 Oct 2025) refused emergency requests to remove her pending litigation.
events.source_title: Trump v. Cook (Wikipedia)

events.summary: Stephen Miran, chair of the White House Council of Economic Advisers, was sworn in as a Fed governor after a 48-47 Senate vote, filling Adriana Kugler's seat; he was the first Fed member to concurrently serve in the executive branch since the 1930s. He resigned from the CEA on 3 Feb 2026.
events.source_title: Stephen Miran (Wikipedia)

events.summary: The Department of Justice served the Federal Reserve with grand jury subpoenas threatening a criminal indictment related to Chair Powell's June 2025 Senate testimony on the renovation of Fed buildings. Powell said in a statement on 11 Jan 2026 that the action should be seen in the context of the administration's threats and pressure.
events.source_title: Statement from Federal Reserve Chair Jerome H. Powell (Federal Reserve Board, 11 Jan 2026)

events.summary: Kevin Warsh took office as Fed Chair for a term ending 21 May 2030, succeeding Jerome Powell, who chaired the Board from 5 Feb 2018 to 22 May 2026. Powell remains listed as a Board member.
events.source_title: Kevin Warsh, Chairman (Federal Reserve Board)

events.summary: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 in Trump v. Cook that Lisa Cook could remain on the Fed Board while her challenge to her removal proceeds, holding that the statute's for-cause protection entitles a governor to notice and an opportunity to respond.
events.source_title: Trump v. Cook (Wikipedia)

events.summary: The White House notified Lisa Cook that Trump was "considering" firing her and gave her three weeks to respond.
events.source_title: Trump v. Cook (Wikipedia)

events.summary: A presidential decree replaced central bank governor Murat Cetinkaya, whose term ran to 2020, with deputy Murat Uysal; Erdogan said Cetinkaya had made decisions for which a high price was paid, after the bank held its rate at 24%.
events.source_title: Turkey's Erdogan urges central bank overhaul: Report (Al Jazeera, 10 Jul 2019)

events.summary: President Erdogan removed governor Murat Uysal by decree in the Official Gazette and appointed former finance minister Naci Agbal, after the lira lost 30% of its value in 2020.
events.source_title: Turkey's Erdogan replaces central bank governor as lira plummets (Al Jazeera, 7 Nov 2020)

events.summary: Erdogan removed governor Naci Agbal by decree after four months in office, following an interest rate rise, and appointed Sahap Kavcioglu, a banking professor who had argued for lower rates.
events.source_title: Turkey's Erdogan sacks central bank governor after rate hike (Al Jazeera, 20 Mar 2021)

events.summary: Governor Sahap Kavcioglu, who had cut rates from 19% to 8.5%, was replaced by Hafize Gaye Erkan by presidential decree.
events.source_title: Şahap Kavcıoğlu (Wikipedia)

events.summary: President Bola Tinubu suspended Central Bank of Nigeria governor Godwin Emefiele with immediate effect, citing an ongoing investigation, and named Deputy Governor Folashodun Shonubi acting governor.
events.source_title: Emefiele Suspended, Shonubi Appointed Acting CBN Governor (ThisDay, 10 Jun 2023)

events.summary: The Tripoli-based Presidential Council issued a decree replacing Central Bank of Libya governor Sadiq al-Kabir, in post since October 2011, with former deputy governor Mohamed Abdul Salam al-Shukri.
events.source_title: Libya's presidential council replaces central bank governor (Arise News, 19 Aug 2024)

events.summary: Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah's government sent a delegation to take over the governor's office; al-Kabir said he and other senior staff fled the country because of militia threats, and banking operations were suspended.
events.source_title: Libya's central bank chief flees country over militia threats: Report (Al Jazeera, 30 Aug 2024)

events.summary: Bangladesh Bank governor Abdur Rouf Talukder resigned citing health reasons, four days after Sheikh Hasina fled the country and three days after more than a hundred central bank officials stormed his office demanding his resignation.
events.source_title: Bangladesh Bank governor resigns (The Daily Star, 9 Aug 2024)

events.summary: National Bank of Ukraine governor Yakiv Smolii submitted his resignation to President Zelensky, stating that "systematic political pressure has been exerted on the National Bank of Ukraine".
events.source_title: National Bank head Yakiv Smolii resigns due to political pressure (Kyiv Post)

events.summary: Central bank governor Tarek Amer, in office since 2015 with a term due to run to 2023, resigned; President al-Sisi accepted the resignation and named him a presidential adviser, with the pound at 19.1 to the dollar.
events.source_title: Egypt central bank chief quits amid deepening crisis (Al-Monitor/AFP, Aug 2022)

events.summary: President Hassan Rouhani's cabinet dismissed central bank governor Abdolnasser Hemmati because of his candidacy in the 18 June presidential election and replaced him with deputy Akbar Komijani.
events.source_title: Iran's central bank chief dismissed for running for president (Al Jazeera, 30 May 2021)

events.summary: President Edgar Lungu dismissed Bank of Zambia governor Denny Kalyalya, less than a week after he warned of economic difficulties, and appointed Christopher Mvunga from the finance ministry.
events.source_title: Zambian president fires central bank governor (Central Banking, 24 Aug 2020)

events.summary: Newly elected President Lazarus Chakwera dismissed Reserve Bank of Malawi governor Dalitso Kabambe and appointed Wilson Banda on 8 July 2020.
events.source_title: Malawi's new president dismisses governor (Central Banking)

events.summary: President Peter Mutharika appointed Henry Mathanga as Reserve Bank of Malawi deputy governor; Mathanga had been dismissed by the bank after a disciplinary inquiry and faces criminal charges, and critics say the appointment breaches Section 16(2) of the RBM Act.
events.source_title: Malawi: Outrage As Mutharika Appoints Fired and Charged Mathanga As RBM Deputy Governor (Nyasa Times via allAfrica, 11 Jan 2026)

events.summary: Sovereignty Council head Abdel Fattah al-Burhan dismissed Central Bank of Sudan governor Burai Al-Siddiq Ali Ahmed after a dispute over gold purchase and export rules and appointed Amna Mirghani Hassan El Toum; deputy governor Mohamed Osman Ahmed Mohamed Khair was dismissed less than two weeks later.
events.source_title: Sudan: Conflicts of Influence and Interests Confound Central Bank of Sudan (Dabanga via allAfrica, 29 Oct 2025)

events.summary: Three days after the 1 Feb 2021 coup, the military's State Administration Council appointed Than Than Swe deputy governor of the Central Bank of Myanmar; she later became governor, replacing Than Nyein.
events.source_title: Than Than Swe (Wikipedia)

events.summary: The military junta replaced Central Bank of Myanmar governor Than Nyein and a vice chairman with Than Than Swe and Major General Zaw Myint Naing, two months after it had appointed six lieutenant colonels as deputy directors of the bank. Radio Free Asia reported the shake-up as a bid by the junta to control the country's financial sector. This is recorded as a removal rather than an appointment: the governor was replaced by the authority that had seized power, not at the end of a term.
events.source_title: Bank shake-up seen as bid by junta to control Myanmar's financial sector (RFA, 24 Aug 2022)

events.summary: After the Taliban takeover, the US froze nearly $9.5bn of Da Afghanistan Bank assets, much held at the New York Federal Reserve, and stopped cash shipments.
events.source_title: US freezes Afghan central bank's assets of $9.5bn (Al Jazeera, 18 Aug 2021)

events.summary: President Biden signed an executive order to split $7bn of frozen Afghan central bank assets: $3.5bn for Afghan relief and $3.5bn kept in the US for litigation by US victims of terrorism.
events.source_title: Biden moves to split $7 billion in frozen Afghan funds for 9/11 victims (AP via KTVU, 11 Feb 2022)

events.summary: After Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Western countries immobilised Russian central bank assets under their jurisdictions, estimated at around EUR 300bn worldwide.
events.source_title: Confiscation of immobilised Russian sovereign assets (European Parliamentary Research Service, 8 Sep 2025)

events.summary: The EU agreed to freeze EUR 210bn of Russian central bank assets held in Europe indefinitely, using Article 122 of the EU treaty, replacing six-monthly renewals that Hungary or Slovakia could veto.
events.source_title: EU agrees to indefinite freeze of Russian assets (Novaya Gazeta Europe, 13 Dec 2025)

events.summary: London's High Court ruled that Venezuelan supreme court judgments backing the Maduro-appointed central bank board should be disregarded, keeping more than $1bn of Venezuelan gold at the Bank of England out of Maduro's control.
events.source_title: London's High Court rules against Venezuela's Maduro in $1 billion gold battle (Reuters via Mining.com, 29 Jul 2022)

events.summary: Former central bank governor Riad Salameh, governor for three decades until 2023, was arrested in Beirut on charges of embezzlement, money laundering and fraud linked to commissions from the bank's dealings with a brokerage firm; he denies wrongdoing.
events.source_title: Former Lebanon central bank chief Riad Salameh arrested amid corruption probe (Semafor, 3 Sep 2024)

events.summary: Ruling-coalition MPs filed a motion to bring National Bank of Poland president Adam Glapiński before the State Tribunal on eight charges, including bond purchases that indirectly financed the budget deficit and unauthorised currency interventions.
events.source_title: Polish ruling coalition moves to put central bank governor on trial (Notes from Poland, 26 Mar 2024)

events.summary: The Sejm's Committee for Constitutional Responsibility backed a 148-page report upholding all eight charges against Glapiński, including PLN 144bn of bond purchases in 2020-21; a full Sejm vote must wait at least 21 days, and indictment could suspend him.
events.source_title: Tusk's parliamentary majority moves to depose head of Polish central bank (Brussels Signal, 12 Oct 2026)

events.summary: The National Bank of Hungary said a proposed government law widening the supervisory board's control over activities outside its basic tasks could erode its independence, amid pressure on Governor Gyorgy Matolcsy to cut rates.
events.source_title: Forint in 'perfect storm' as Hungary's central bank rebuffs law change (Reuters via Swissinfo, 12 Mar 2024)

events.summary: The government proposed amendments to the central bank law that would ban the MNB from creating new foundations, add a fourth deputy governor and expand the monetary policy committee from nine to 11 members.
events.source_title: Hungary to change central bank law (Central Banking, 14 May 2025)

events.summary: President Javier Milei announced a bill to reform the BCRA charter to restore a single mandate of preserving the currency's value, bar money issuance to finance the state and primary-market purchases of government bonds, and restrict profit transfers to the Treasury to debt repayment.
events.source_title: Cinco claves de la reforma del Banco Central y el 'grillete' fiscal impulsados por Milei (EFE via ABC Color, 30 Jul 2026)

events.summary: President Lula called central bank president Roberto Campos Neto his "political and ideological adversary" and said that when he could replace him at year-end Brazil would return "to normality".
events.source_title: Campos Neto é 'adversário político e ideológico', diz Lula (Poder360, 21 Jun 2024)

events.summary: President Gustavo Petro accused the Banco de la República of wanting to "finish off the economy" and of having an electoral bet after its board voted 4-3 to hold the rate at 9.25%.
events.source_title: Petro acusa al Banco de la República de tener una apuesta electoral (Publimetro, 31 Jul 2025)

events.summary: President López Obrador withdrew his nomination of former finance minister Arturo Herrera as Banco de México governor and nominated deputy finance secretary Victoria Rodríguez Ceja.
events.source_title: ¿Por qué AMLO retiró candidatura de Arturo Herrera al Banco de México? (Por Esto, 24 Nov 2021)

events.summary: Finance Minister Chris Sinckler fired Governor Delisle Worrell. The government's stated reason was that the board objected to his reported high-handed manner. Some observers believed the reason was his refusal to keep financing the government with new money: his January letter said the government must stop taking new money from the bank to pay its bills. The Appeals Court upheld the minister's right to dismiss him.
events.source_title: Barbados Central Bank governor fired (Caribbean Life)

events.summary: A junta court sentenced former deputy governor Bo Bo Nge to 20 years in prison in December 2022 after a months-long secret trial, sources said for "mismanagement of banks trading foreign currency". The junta-backed Anti-Corruption Commission accused him of not collecting tax on a $5 million Open Society deposit and of placing a $350 million loan in a lower-interest account, with alleged losses of 102, 360 and 655 million kyats. He was arrested on the morning of the February 2021 coup, and economist Sean Turnell called him someone "fighting against corruption".
events.source_title: Myanmar junta sentences former Central Bank official to 20 years in prison (RFA)

events.summary: The government called on Martin Redrado to resign on 6 January, saying he refused to back its decree calling for $6.6 billion of reserves; he refused to go. On 7 January President Kirchner issued a second decree firing him and accusing him of misconduct. On 8 January the courts suspended both decrees.
events.source_title: The end of the Redrado era: a timeline (Euromoney)

events.summary: President Goodluck Jonathan suspended central bank governor Sanusi Lamido Sanusi. The president's aide cited "various acts of financial recklessness". Sanusi had reported the year before that $50bn of oil sold by the state oil company NNPC had not been paid to the government; NNPC repeatedly denied his allegations, and he could not be reached for comment on the suspension.
events.source_title: Nigeria president suspends central bank chief (Al Jazeera)

events.summary: Reserve Bank of India governor Urjit Patel resigned, saying only that it was for personal reasons. Media reports said he was annoyed by repeated government efforts to influence central bank policy, after a public spat over alleged interference. Finance Minister Arun Jaitley responded by acknowledging Patel's time at the bank with appreciation.
events.source_title: India's central bank chief quits after spat with government (Dawn)

events.summary: Central Bank of Iraq governor Sinan Al Shabibi was removed and a successor named, during a parliamentary probe into possible manipulation of the dinar against the dollar. A committee member said arrest warrants had been issued for 30 people including Al Shabibi and his deputy, Mudher Saleh. The integrity committee chairman said the probe was "not about money, but about procedures"; a finance committee member called it "a political decision and not professional". The article reports no statement from Al Shabibi.
events.source_title: Iraq central bank chief sacked and sought for arrest in currency dispute (The National)

events.summary: The Thai government fired central bank governor Chatu Mongol Sonakul. Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra said he was not satisfied with the bank's policy of keeping interest rates low. The readable part of the article, which is cut off by a paywall, carries no response from the governor.
events.source_title: Thai government sacks central bank boss (Central Banking)

events.summary: Central Bank of Cyprus governor Panicos Demetriades resigned, to leave on 10 April, with no reason given. The president had earlier said he would begin proceedings to have him removed for not doing his job properly; at the resignation a government statement thanked him for helping prevent the country's bankruptcy. The article carries no statement from Demetriades on the dispute.
events.source_title: Cyprus central bank governor resigns amid simmering dispute with president (Fox News)

events.summary: Iran replaced central bank governor Valiollah Seif, in post since August 2013, with Abdolnasser Hemati. The article gives no stated reason for the removal: President Hassan Rouhani thanked Seif for his "strong and serious service" and said a key priority was tackling "illegal credit institutions". It records no statement from Seif.
events.source_title: Iran sacks central bank chief, as rial's slide continues (The New Arab)

events.summary: Bank Indonesia governor Syahril was released after six months of detention when prosecutors' detention orders expired. He still faced corruption charges and a possible life sentence over his alleged involvement in the 546 billion rupiah Bank Bali scandal, while the administration was pushing to remove him and install its own candidates. A presidential spokesman said "This release merely follows legal procedures". A Jakarta court later sentenced him to three years in 2002, and in 2004 Kyodo, quoting a senior Supreme Court judge, reported the top court had rejected prosecutors' appeal and acquitted him on all charges (Central Banking, 1 Oct 2004: centralbanking.com/node/1411040).
events.source_title: Syahril back at helm of central bank (The Straits Times, via Asia Pacific Solidarity Network)

events.summary: President Joyce Banda removed Reserve Bank of Malawi governor Perks Ligoya, according to two unnamed sources, with Charles Chuka reportedly chosen to succeed him. No official reason was stated; the reporter described it as her latest move to clean house and woo donors back. No one at the central bank was available for comment.
events.source_title: New Malawi president sacks central bank chief (Nampa-Reuters, The Namibian)

events.summary: Central Bank of Kenya governor Andrew Mullei was sacked for abuse of office; the article says he appointed investigators to the Charterhouse Bank probe without following due process. He fought in court and his name was cleared, too late to get his job back because a replacement had already been appointed.
events.source_title: Jinxed: CBK governor post which has caused past holders untold grief (The EastAfrican)

events.summary: Central Bank of Kenya governor Micah Cheserem was dismissed in 2001 and replaced by Nahashon Nyagah. The article says he became a pawn in political battles; it gives no reason stated by the government. Cheserem is quoted saying political interests are the driving force behind the woes governors face.
events.source_title: Jinxed: CBK governor post which has caused past holders untold grief (The EastAfrican)

events.summary: Sierra Leone's recently elected president dismissed the governor of the central bank, and Kelfala Kallon was appointed on 15 August as the bank's third governor in 17 months. The readable part of the article, cut off by a paywall, does not name the dismissed governor or give either side's reason.
events.source_title: Sierra Leone's president fires governor and appoints successor (Central Banking)

events.summary: President Bio sent Bank of Sierra Leone governor Kelfala Kallon on "indefinite leave" and named deputy Ibrahim Stevens interim head. The advisory firm that wrote this article reports no official reason and no response from Kallon; it says the president tried to bypass the 2019 Bank of Sierra Leone Act, under which sacking the governor needs a two-thirds majority in parliament.
events.source_title: Sierra Leone's central bank governor removed months to elections (Songhai Advisory)

events.summary: Claim, not confirmed: Daily News Egypt reported that severe pressure, from no named person or body, pushed Central Bank of Egypt governor Hisham Ramez to resign more than a month before his tenure ended. Ramez made no direct statement; unnamed colleagues said he did not want to stay and preferred to leave.
events.source_title: Pressure pushed Ramez to resign a month before end of tenure (Daily News Egypt)

events.summary: President Nicolas Maduro announced the firing of Central Bank chief Nelson Merentes, who the article says handed in his resignation, and named economist Ricardo Sanguino to succeed him. The article reports no reason from Maduro and no statement from Merentes; it places the firing amid an economic crisis and a bungled release of larger banknotes.
events.source_title: Maduro sacks the head of Venezuela's central bank (PTI, Business Standard)

events.summary: Parliament voted no confidence in National Bank of Ukraine head Volodymyr Stelmakh, with 227 of 450 seats in favour. Parliament cited a fall of nearly half in the hryvna's value since November, a shrinking economy and rising deficits. President Yushchenko's office called the decision "illegal" and repeated its support for Stelmakh.
events.source_title: Ukraine president says sacking of national bank boss illegal (UNIAN)

events.summary: The Hungarian cabinet decided to go ahead with a draft bill cutting National Bank governor András Simor's monthly pay by 75%, from about Ft 8 million to Ft 2 million, through a cap on everyone paid from public funds. A government spokesman said this did not threaten the bank's independence because it applied to the whole public sector. The ECB said such changes should apply only to future appointments and be made in consultation with the bank. The article has no statement from Simor.
events.source_title: Hungarian Cabinet Rejects ECB Warning Over MNB Pay Cuts (Hungary Around the Clock, via XpatLoop)

events.summary: President Moncef Marzouki fired central bank governor Mustapha Kamel Nabli, alleging he had refused to bring monetary policy in line with the country's economic needs. The elected assembly approved the move in July 2012. The article carries no statement from Nabli.
events.source_title: Tunisia assembly backs central bank head firing (AP, Washington Examiner)

events.summary: Central Bank of Belize governor Gustavo Manuel Vasquez lost his post. Prime Minister John Briceño said the board recommended he resign because of "a lot of policy differences". Vasquez wrote that his appointment was terminated on the instructions of the Ministry of Finance, that he faced opposition from it, and that he had tried to restore the bank's integrity and operational autonomy.
events.source_title: PM: CBB governor fired for differences with board (The Reporter, Belize)

events.summary: The MDC, partner in the power-sharing government, demanded that Reserve Bank governor Gideon Gono be replaced, saying Western donors would not fund reconstruction until he was. President Mugabe said Gono would stay: "Prove the wrong he has done." Gono has no direct quote; he reportedly sought protection from "personal attacks" by Finance Minister Tendai Biti. Gono was not removed in this account.
events.source_title: Zimbabwe's Mugabe Vows Not to Remove Beleaguered Central Bank Chief (VOA)

events.summary: President Maithripala Sirisena said in a speech that he personally removed Central Bank governor Arjuna Mahendran, saying the decision served the national interest and linking it to the appointment of Indrajit Coomaraswamy. The date is when he said this; the article does not give the date of the removal, and has no statement from Mahendran.
events.source_title: President takes credit for sacking Arjuna Mahendran (Daily FT)

events.summary: Guillermo Aponte became interim president of the Banco Central de Bolivia, replacing Pablo Ramos, who was under investigation for alleged favouring of illicit enrichment. The questions covered armoured trucks said to have taken foreign currency out of the bank at unusual hours and about $75 million in loans to state firms. Transitional president Jeanine Áñez said the bank "recupera la autonomía de decisión"; the article has no statement from Ramos. Status: under investigation.
events.source_title: Un nuevo presidente reemplaza al investigado en el Banco Central de Bolivia (EFE, Diario Libre)

events.summary: The government dismissed governor Maria do Carmo Silveira, a former prime minister, and her team, citing irregularities in the construction of the new central bank building, valued at US$8 million. The article, cut off on the page, does not mention corruption or fraud.
events.source_title: Sao Tome government fires central bank governor (Central Banking)

events.summary: Central bank head Carlos Carvallo resigned at the request of President Santiago Peña, who said he asked "in light of facts that emerged throughout the day", including a prosecutor's request for a criminal investigation around the digital lender ueno and orders to arrest eight people linked to it. Carvallo said stepping aside would help quell the controversy around the bank. He headed ueno until August 2023; Peña was a business partner of the group that owned it until March 2025.
events.source_title: Paraguay's central bank chief resigns at president's request as digital lender crisis deepens (The Star)

events.summary: President Nicanor Duarte Frutos dismissed Central Bank president Mónica Pérez, a former IMF official in post since June 2005. An unnamed official source said the reason was her constant disagreements with the rest of the government's economic team. The article carries no response from Pérez.
events.source_title: Presidente paraguaio destitui presidente do Banco Central (Jornal do Brasil)

events.summary: President Nursultan Nazarbayev replaced National Bank chairman Kayrat Kelimbetov with presidential adviser Daniyar Akishev. Nazarbayev told parliament confidence in the bank and the tenge had fallen and that a shortage of tenge liquidity was being felt. The article carries no statement from Kelimbetov.
events.source_title: Kazakhstan: Currency woes hasten central bank boss' demise (Eurasianet)

events.summary: President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi, announcing from Saudi Arabia, sacked central bank head Mohammed bin Hammam, named Mansar al-Kaiti in his place and ordered the bank moved to Aden. The article quotes no official reason and no response from bin Hammam or the Houthis; it describes the move as one that would raise pressure on the Houthi rebels who hold the capital.
events.source_title: Yemeni leader relocates central bank in blow to rebels (Al Jazeera)

events.summary: On the evening of December 21 parliament dismissed National Bank governor Octavian Armașu, in post since November 2018, with 81 MPs in favour, after hearings on recovering money stolen from the banking system. The decision cited "insufficient and defective work" by the bank in examining the bank fraud case. The article carries no response from Armașu.
events.source_title: Octavian Armașu dismissed from post of National Bank governor (IPN)

events.summary: Finance Minister Kittiratt Na-Ranong said Bank of Thailand governor Prasarn Trairatvorakul should be replaced because he had not cut the repurchase rate to curb the baht's rise, calling the 2.75% rate too high. Prasarn was unavailable for comment. Korn Chatikavanij said Kittiratt should not have spoken out, as it could erode investor confidence.
events.source_title: Kittiratt wants central bank chief replaced (Bangkok Post)

events.summary: Parliament voted 80 to 19 to move banking supervision from the National Bank to a new Financial Supervisory Agency, on a draft from two Georgian Dream MPs. Co-author Tamaz Mechiauri reportedly argued that the National Bank board's composition was against the current leadership's interests and that the change would discourage currency speculation. Bidzina Ivanishvili blamed the bank and its chairman Giorgi Kadagidze for the lari's fall; the article carries no statement from Kadagidze.
events.source_title: Georgia's new banking law draws criticism (RFE/RL)

events.summary: Parliament approved President Ilham Aliyev's proposal to replace Central Bank governor Elman Rustamov, in post since 1995, with Pasha Bank chief Taleh Kazimov. Rustamov was then made adviser to the prime minister. The article reports no official reason and no statement from Rustamov.
events.source_title: Aliyev replaces long-serving central bank head with loyalist (OC Media)

events.summary: President Daniel Chapo revoked the appointment of Waldemar Fernando de Sousa as Bank of Mozambique governor "due to subsequent circumstances", which the statement did not specify, and named Felisberto Dinis Navalha instead. The article says Chapo may have backed down after public criticism, because the Attorney General's Office accuses De Sousa of involvement in the hidden debts scandal; he was not tried in the main case. The article reports no response from him.
events.source_title: Chapo reverses De Sousa's appointment and names Dinis Navalha as Bank of Mozambique new governor (AIM)

events.summary: President Filipe Nyusi fired central bank deputy governor António Pinto de Abreu, in post since December 2010. The president's office gave no reason.
events.source_title: Mozambique's Nyusi fires deputy central bank governor: presidency (Yahoo Finance)

events.summary: Bank of Mongolia governor Naidansuren Zoljargal, governor since 2012, was replaced by Bayartsaikhan Nadmid two years before his term was due to end. The visible part of the article does not say who confirmed the appointment and says no reason was given.
events.source_title: Mongolia governor replaced two years before end of term (Central Banking)

events.summary: The Daily Graphic reported the government was pushing for the exit of Bank of Ghana second deputy governor Johnson Asiama. His counsel alleged that some government officials had told him they wanted him to step aside; Asiama said he had not resigned. The article reports no official government reason and no final outcome.
events.source_title: 2nd Deputy BoG Governor in showdown with govt (Daily Graphic)

events.summary: Isaac Adongo, speaking for the Minority in Parliament, said governor Ernest Addison had been "incompetent" over the cedi's fall and inflation and should resign or be sacked. He said Addison had borrowed "in excess of 7billion dollars" on the bank's balance sheet to support the cedi and claimed the government had borrowed illegally through the bank. The article reports no answer from the governor or the government.
events.source_title: Resign or be sacked, Minority tells BoG's Governor (MyJoyOnline)

events.summary: Claim, not confirmed: MP Kwasi Ameyaw-Cheremeh said the government forced Bank of Ghana governor Henry Kofi Wampah out over embarrassment including the micro-finance crisis in Brong Ahafo. Wampah said he had agreed with President Mahama to leave at the end of March, ahead of his August term end, so a successor could settle in before the elections. The article reports no government response.
events.source_title: BoG Governor was forced to resign - MP (Daily Post)

events.summary: In a speech announcing the 2017 budget, President Rodrigo Duterte told the central bank governor Amando Tetangco "I will give you a whack" and threatened criminal charges against the Anti-Money Laundering Council, which Tetangco chairs, accusing it of not tracking drug money, without details on the alleged corruption. Tetangco did not immediately respond; Deputy Governor Diwa Guinigundo said the bank was independent.
events.source_title: Philippines' Duterte wants to give bank Governor 'a whack', charge staff (Daily FT)

events.summary: Governor Arjuna Mahendran's term ended on 30 June; he told the Monetary Board he would not seek reappointment until the parliamentary committee COPE finished its Treasury bond probe. President Maithripala Sirisena, who said in June 2015 that Mahendran should resign, tweeted he would appoint a new governor within hours, while Prime Minister Ranil Wickremesinghe said Mahendran could not be removed because the charges "had never been proved". The Auditor General found a Rs. 1.6 billion loss; no new governor was announced that day.
events.source_title: Political tug-o-war over CB Governor (Daily FT)

events.summary: La Paz prosecutors ordered the arrest of former Banco Central president Edwin Rojas and three former executives, investigated for breach of duties and uneconomic conduct over a 2024 regulation that the prosecutor says allowed irregular sovereign bond transactions, with alleged damage of $us 124 million. Rojas invoked his right to silence. The article does not say whether they have been formally charged.
events.source_title: Aprehenden al expresidente y tres exejecutivos del Banco Central (Los Tiempos)

events.summary: State Bank of Pakistan governor Yaseen Anwar resigned. The Finance Ministry spokesman said he cited personal reasons; unnamed senior officials said that was a cover for differences with Finance Minister Ishaq Dar over inflation and reserves, and that he was unhappy with a recent deputy governor appointment. The article reports no government pressure.
events.source_title: State Bank governor resigns, cites personal reasons (Dawn)

events.summary: Parliament approved the resignation letter of National Bank head Kubanychbek Bokontaev, in post since 2021, relieving him ahead of schedule. The article gives no reason from either side.
events.source_title: Parliament of Kyrgyzstan relieves head of National Bank of his post (24.kg)

events.summary: President Néstor Kirchner's government was to replace central bank president Alfonso Prat-Gay, whose term ended that week, with Martin Redrado, subject to Senate approval. The article says the trigger was unclear; local media suggested disagreements over the debt restructuring. Neither side is quoted.
events.source_title: Argentine Central Bank chiefs to go (MercoPress)

events.summary: A bill expected to pass on July 15 would place the National Bank of Serbia under government control and allow the dismissal of governor Mladjan Dinkic. The article reports the government side's complaints: Prime Minister Zoran Djindjic wanted a devaluation Dinkic resisted, and DOS members said a party official cannot be governor. Dinkic said the law would make the bank dependent on government and parliament; authorities said his claims had no foundation.
events.source_title: Serbia: central bank bill and Dinkic (IWPR)

events.summary: Bangladesh Bank governor Atiur Rahman resigned after an $81m hack, saying he was "ready to resign from my post for the sake of the country". He had been criticised for not telling the finance minister about the loss, and Finance Minister Abul Maal Abdul Muhith called the bank's handling very incompetent. The article does not say the government asked him to go.
events.source_title: Bangladesh Bank governor resigns after $81m hack (Al Jazeera)

events.summary: Bank Negara Malaysia governor Ahmad Mohd Don and his deputy Fong Weng Phak resigned in late August 1998, during the Asian financial crisis, in disagreement with the government's currency plans. Ahmad Don had favoured tight monetary policy and was backed by Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim, while Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad and Daim Zainuddin wanted an expansionary course; Mahathir and Daim had attacked the governor publicly over the tight policy. Reporting at the time said a row over the implementation of comprehensive and unorthodox currency controls prompted the two resignations, and that the central bank had sided with Anwar in the dispute. Anwar was sacked days later. Zeti Akhtar Aziz was appointed acting governor on 31 August 1998, and capital controls, a ringgit peg to the dollar and a freeze on repatriating foreign portfolio capital followed on 1 September.
events.source_title: Lifetime achievement award: Zeti Akhtar Aziz (Central Banking)

events.summary: President Boris Yeltsin fired Central Bank chairman Viktor Gerashchenko for his role in the Black Tuesday ruble crash and appointed Tatyana Paramonova. The State Duma then rejected her in a secret ballot, 107 to 127; opponents said the constitution barred hiring or firing the bank's chief without Duma approval.
events.source_title: Parliament rejects Yeltsin's bank chief (The Moscow Times)

events.summary: Valeria Gontareva stepped down as governor of the National Bank of Ukraine on 10 May 2017, but parliament had still not voted on her resignation or on a replacement by January 2018. President Petro Poroshenko nominated acting head Yakiv Smolii on 18 January 2018. Gontareva had been on unpaid leave since 26 September, saying she would stay away until parliament acted.
events.source_title: Ukraine: outgoing central bank governor urges parliament, president to let her go at last (bne IntelliNews)

events.summary: Yemen's president Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi dismissed the governor of the Central Bank of Yemen and his deputy, according to state news agency Saba. Ahmed bin Ahmed Ghaleb Al-Maabq was named governor and Muhammad Omar Banaja deputy. The page gives no reason, and describes it as the fourth such sacking since the civil war began.
events.source_title: Yemeni governor sacked as crisis worsens (Central Banking)

events.summary: Mongolian lawmakers accepted the resignation of central bank governor Nadmid Bayartsaikhan on 21 November 2019. The page, citing Xinhua, says he resigned after the Financial Action Task Force added Mongolia to its grey list over money-laundering enforcement. Parliament appointed Byadran Lkhagvasuren the next day.
events.source_title: New Mongolian governor appointed amid AML controversy (Central Banking)

events.summary: Dorin Dragutanu announced his resignation as governor of the National Bank of Moldova after criticism for failing to prevent about $1 billion disappearing from three Moldovan banks in 2014. He said he was resigning because of pressure from some politicians and denied responsibility, saying he had repeatedly warned authorities. President Nicolae Timofti and Prime Minister Valeriu Strelet had both said he should be removed.
events.source_title: Moldovan Central Bank Governor Resigns (RFE/RL)

events.summary: Melis Turgunbaev, chairman of the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic since 26 June 2024, submitted a resignation letter, which Speaker Marlen Mamataliev announced in a session of the Zhogorku Kenesh (parliament). The page calls it a voluntary resignation and gives no reason for it.
events.source_title: Head of Kyrgyzstan's National Bank submits letter of resignation (24.kg)

events.summary: The Banco Central de Bolivia dismissed more than a dozen senior managers, including the manager for international operations, the principal adviser on political economy, and subdirectors of several departments. A former governor said the dismissals were likely influenced by the change of government. The page does not say the governor himself was removed.
events.source_title: Bolivia's central bank sheds senior staff (Central Banking)

events.summary: President Filipe Nyusi appointed IMF official Rogerio Zandamela governor of the Bank of Mozambique, replacing Ernesto Gove after 10 years in the post. The government statement was issued on 31 August 2016. The page gives no reason for the replacement, noting only that the economy continued to slide.
events.source_title: Mozambique replaces governor Gove with IMF official (Central Banking)

events.summary: Bank of Thailand chairman Virabongsa Ramangkura pointed to the cabinet's power under Section 28/19 of the Bank of Thailand Act to remove the governor, then Prasarn Trairatvorakul, during a dispute with Finance Minister Kittiratt Na-Ranong. The page says Virabongsa stopped short of directly calling for the governor's removal, and gives no date.
events.source_title: Bank of Thailand chairman says government can fire governor (Bangkok Post)

events.summary: Governor Mladjan Dinkic resigned from Serbia's central bank, along with two of its three deputy governors, after parliament passed legislation he said undermines the bank's independence. The page says the law gives members of parliament the power to nominate and appoint top central bank officials. Energy Minister Kori Udovicki was nominated as the new governor.
events.source_title: Serbian central bank governor resigns over new law (Central Banking)

events.summary: Argentina's central bank chief Martin Perez Redrado resigned on a Friday amid a dispute with President Cristina Kirchner, in a page dated 30 January 2010. The page says an Argentine court determined that Kirchner needed the approval of the full Congress to use the bank's reserves, and that the reserves remained frozen while lawmakers were expected to take up the matter in March.
events.source_title: Argentine chief banker resigns but foreign reserves remain frozen (MercoPress)

events.summary: Pheu Thai Party leader Paetongtarn Shinawatra criticised the Bank of Thailand's independence, saying the law making it independent of the government obstructs solving economic problems. The remarks drew a backlash, and Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin said he had no plans to remove Governor Sethaput Suthiwartnarueput or amend the Bank of Thailand Act. The page says the 2008 amendment to that Act makes removing the governor over policy disagreements very difficult.
events.source_title: Why Thailand's central bank governor is hard to remove (The Nation Thailand)

events.summary: Bank of Ghana governor Abdul Nashiru Issahaku resigned, effective after 1 April 2017, telling Joy Business he was leaving for personal reasons; the page says the decision came out of an agreement reached with the government earlier that month. His job had come under scrutiny after the New Patriotic Party won the 2016 election, and NPP figure Anthony Akoto Osei held that he should voluntarily step down. The page notes the governor's four-year term is protected by Article 183(4)(d) of the 1992 constitution.
events.source_title: Bank of Ghana Governor resigns (MyJoyOnline)

events.summary: In September 2003 members of Jordan's parliament signed a petition urging Prime Minister Ali Abulragheb to remove Central Bank of Jordan governor Umayya Touqan, after Touqan froze all bank accounts belonging to six leaders of Hamas. The report does not say whether the government acted on the petition.
events.source_title: Jordan central bank chief rebuked over bank freeze (Central Banking)

events.summary: Madagascar's transitional government dismissed central bank governor Frederic Rasamoely in February 2012. Bank employees staged a sit-in, saying the removal contravened the bank's independence, and said the strike would continue while they challenged the new governor's appointment.
events.source_title: Madagascan central bank staff revolt, reports say (Central Banking)

events.summary: Hurriyet Daily News reported that Hungary's government moved to demote central bank governor Andras Simor by merging the Magyar Nemzeti Bank with the financial regulator. Under a constitutional amendment tabled by parliament's constitutional committee on 14 December 2011, the merged body would be headed by a person appointed by President Pal Schmitt on Prime Minister Viktor Orban's nomination, and Simor would be reduced to deputy head. Parliament was due to vote on 16 December 2011. Simor said he refused to give in to what he called "bullying" by the government to leave his post before his mandate ended in March 2013. The report also says that earlier in 2011 the government changed the rules for appointing Monetary Council members, removing Simor's influence over who the external members would be. An opposition Socialist member of the committee, Gergely Barandy, said the proposal was "nothing but a re-staffing proposal hidden in a structural change idea."
events.source_title: Hungary seeks to demote bank chief (Hurriyet Daily News)

events.summary: Thai PBS World reported on 10 November 2024 that the selection committee for the chair of the Bank of Thailand's board was choosing between three candidates, and that the government's nominee was Kittiratt Na-Ranong, a former finance minister and deputy prime minister under Yingluck Shinawatra. The report describes Kittiratt as a Pheu Thai Party loyalist and a staunch critic of the central bank governor, Sethaput Suthiwartnarueput. More than 800 academics and economists, four former central bank governors and former bank officials signed a statement opposing the appointment, saying: "We are deeply concerned about the implications of political intervention on monetary policy." The report notes that the board chair appoints four of the seven members of the Monetary Policy Committee and takes part in choosing the next governor, whose term was due to end in September 2025, and that the decision on the chair had already been deferred twice. The dispute followed the central bank cutting its policy rate to 2.25% while the government pressed for a further cut.
events.source_title: With Kittiratt card, govt threatens BOT's independence (Thai PBS World)

events.summary: Fox News, in a report dated 11 January 2014, said President Gurbanguly Berdymukhamedov dismissed the head of Turkmenistan's central bank, Tuvakmammet Japarov, along with the chiefs of two other state-run banks. State television announced the firings. The stated reason was unspecified "flaws in their work." The report adds that the president had earlier reprimanded Japarov and other bankers for taking regular bonuses and had ordered them to repay the money. The same round of dismissals also removed the head of the state gas company Turkmengaz.
events.source_title: Turkmenistan president fires central bank chief, other officials (Fox News)

events.summary: Euromoney reported on 1 November 2005 that Ulan Sarbanov, governor of Kyrgyzstan's central bank, had been placed under house arrest in the course of a government investigation. The investigation concerned funds he transferred to the previous president, Askar Akayev, in 1999. The report does not state the specific charge and does not say wrongdoing was proven. It says Sarbanov's position had been insecure since Akayev was ousted in March 2005, and that politicians close to the new leader, Kurmanbek Bakiyev, had pressed for Sarbanov's dismissal.
events.source_title: Kyrgyzstan: Central banker under house arrest (Euromoney)

events.summary: Radio Tamazuj reported that on Monday 9 June 2025 President Salva Kiir Mayardit removed Johnny Ohisa Domian as governor of the Bank of South Sudan by presidential decree, broadcast on state-run media. The bank's first deputy governor, Addis Ababa Othow, was named to replace him. The report says no reason was given for the dismissal. It notes that the country was facing severe shortages of local currency cash and months of unpaid government salaries, but does not link those to the removal.
events.source_title: South Sudan's president fires central bank governor (Radio Tamazuj)

events.summary: African News Agency reported on 8 December 2021 that Guinea's military leader, Mamadi Doumbouya, dismissed Laounceny Kaba, who had headed the Central Bank of the Republic of Guinea for ten years, together with the two vice-governors, Baidy Aribot and Madjou Sow. A younger economist, Karamo Kaba, was appointed in his place. The report attributes the removal to the length of time Laounceny Kaba had held the post and to his closeness to the deposed president, Alpha Conde, and says he had made unsuccessful attempts to win the junta's confidence. The report presents that last point as a report rather than a confirmed fact; it gives no exact date for the dismissal.
events.source_title: Guinea junta fires Central Bank governor (African News Agency)

events.summary: The Associated Press, carried by ABC News, reported that Libya's Tripoli-based presidential council, allied with Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah's government, issued a decree firing Sadiq al-Kabir as governor of the Central Bank of Libya. Al-Kabir had led the bank since October 2011. The council named Mohamed Abdul Salam al-Shukri, an economist and former deputy governor, to replace him. The report says the decree was issued late on a Sunday and gives no official reason for the firing. The dispute was over who has the authority to appoint the governor: the east-based House of Representatives and the Supreme Council of State, both of which are mandated to appoint central bank governors under the constitutional document, called the firing illegitimate.
events.source_title: Libya's powerful central bank governor is fired as country's deep divisions persist (ABC News / Associated Press)

events.summary: The Associated Press, carried by Fox News, reported that Dorin Dragutanu stepped down as governor of the National Bank of Moldova on Monday 21 September 2015, after weeks of street protests over $1.5 billion that disappeared from three Moldovan banks. Protesters had been camping in a Chisinau square since 6 September and demanded an investigation into the money, which vanished before a parliamentary election the previous November. The report says Dragutanu accused politicians of interfering in the bank's internal affairs and said they had tried to discredit the central bank.
events.source_title: Moldova's central bank governor quits after protest over $1.5 bln which disappeared from banks (Fox News / Associated Press)

events.summary: At a Conservative leadership debate in Edmonton on 11 May 2022, Pierre Poilievre, the front-runner and later party leader, pledged to fire Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem if he became prime minister, saying at the end of the debate: "I will fire the governor of the central bank to get inflation under control." He had called the bank "financially illiterate" the month before, and also promised to have it audited and to bar it from issuing a digital currency. Macklem had been appointed in 2020 to a seven-year term; the Bank of Canada Act says the governor is appointed for seven years "during good behaviour", and commentators noted that removing one would require Parliament's involvement. Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and Finance Minister Chrystia Freeland both publicly defended the bank's independence, and former governor David Dodge rejected the criticism. The party's own finance critic, Ed Fast, was removed from that role after saying publicly that the pledge was deeply troubling and hurt the party's economic credibility. Poilievre repeated the commitment as leader in December 2022.
events.source_title: Frontrunner for Canada's Conservative leadership promises to fire central bank governor

events.summary: On 14 July 2023 Treasurer Jim Chalmers and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced that Reserve Bank of Australia governor Philip Lowe would not be reappointed and would leave when his seven-year term ended on 17 September, after 43 years at the bank. Deputy governor Michele Bullock was appointed in his place. Lowe had been heavily criticised, particularly in the media, after telling the public that rates were unlikely to rise before 2024 and then raising the cash rate from 0.1 to 4.1 percent. That criticism led Chalmers to commission an independent review of the central bank, which recommended sweeping changes to how it is run and how policy is made, and which the government accepted in full. The previous two governors had each been reappointed to a further term as a matter of custom; asked why Lowe was not, Chalmers said extending a governor's tenure was "the exception rather than the rule" and that Bullock was best placed to implement the review.
events.source_title: Australia appoints first female head for central bank (Reuters, via Inquirer Business)

events.summary: Adrian Orr resigned as governor of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand on 5 March 2025, with three years left to run of his second five-year term. Board chair Neil Quigley said at the time that it was a personal decision and would not elaborate. Documents released in June 2025 under the Official Information Act showed the cause was an impasse over the bank's next five-year funding agreement: Orr argued that what Finance Minister Nicola Willis and the Treasury proposed was considerably below what the bank needed, and the board was willing to accept less than he was. The bank said the disagreement was distressing to Orr and risked damaging the working relationship. Orr had sought $1.031 billion; in mid-April Willis confirmed a package of nearly $776 million, about 8 percent more than the previous five years. In August 2025 the Ombudsman compelled the bank to disclose that Orr had temporarily stepped down on 27 February, as tensions with the board, the Treasury and the minister came to a head, and that he agreed to resign on the basis that a letter of concerns from the board was withdrawn. Quigley resigned as board chair on 29 August 2025 after five months of scrutiny over the handling of the departure.
events.source_title: Documents reveal why Adrian Orr suddenly quit as Reserve Bank Governor (RNZ)

events.summary: Before and after taking office in December 2012, Prime Minister Shinzo Abe repeatedly threatened to revise the 1998 Bank of Japan Law, which guarantees the bank's independence in monetary policy, unless the bank adopted a 2 percent inflation target. On 23 December 2012 he said his government would consider revising the Act if the bank did not adopt the target at its January meeting, and that if it refused, "we have to amend the BoJ law, reach an accord and we will have the policy". His party and its coalition partner held a two-thirds majority in the lower house, enough to overrule the upper house on such a bill, so the threat was credible; reporting at the time noted a revision could have given the government power to impose a binding target on the bank or to remove its governor. Lawmakers had already summoned governor Masaaki Shirakawa to the Diet several times in February 2012 to criticise his caution. The bank adopted the 2 percent target and an open-ended asset purchase commitment on 22 January 2013, in a joint statement with the government. Officials inside the bank described the outcome as fending off the most serious threat to its independence in fifteen years, and the government's chief spokesman then said there was less need to revise the law. In February 2013 Abe told parliament that if the bank could not responsibly deliver results, "we would have to consider revising the BoJ law".
events.source_title: Japan's Abe heaps pressure on BOJ to set 2 percent inflation target (Reuters, via Fox Business)

events.summary: On 19 June 2017 the Public Protector, Busisiwe Mkhwebane, published a report on a 1.125 billion rand loan the South African Reserve Bank had made to Bankorp, and included remedial action directing Parliament's justice committee to amend section 224 of the Constitution so as to change the Reserve Bank's mandate, moving it away from protecting the value of the currency and towards economic growth and citizens' socio-economic rights. Under South African law such remedial action is binding unless a court sets it aside, so the Reserve Bank brought an urgent review. Governor Lesetja Kganyago called the instruction a gross overreach. The North Gauteng High Court set the mandate instruction aside on 15 August 2017 and declared it unconstitutional, and in February 2018 a second judgment set aside the rest of the report, finding the remedial action unlawful and that there was a reasonable apprehension of bias. The High Court ordered Mkhwebane to pay 15 percent of the bank's costs personally on a punitive scale, with her office paying the remainder; the Constitutional Court upheld that order on 22 July 2019, while dismissing the bank's separate application for a declaration that she had abused her office. Parliament and the finance minister also went to court against the instruction.
events.source_title: Public Protector's remedial action on Reserve Bank's mandate is set aside by High Court (TimesLIVE)

events.summary: During the Conservative leadership contest, Liz Truss said she would review the Bank of England's mandate if she became prime minister, first raising it at a campaign event in Cardiff on 3 August 2022. Her campaign said that after 25 years she believed it was right to ensure the mandate was fit for purpose, and that she would be more directive in setting it; Suella Braverman, who was backing her, said the review would consider the bank's independence. Truss and her allies repeatedly criticised governor Andrew Bailey's handling of inflation. Bailey publicly defended independence as one of the great virtues of the system and said he would not be drawn into the leadership contest, while indicating he was open to a review of the mandate. The shadow chancellor called the proposal deeply irresponsible, and Truss's rival Rishi Sunak said the discussion could spook international investors. Once in office Truss backed the bank's authority to set interest rates and dropped mention of a review. The argument returned later: a group of 44 Conservative MPs, among them Jacob Rees-Mogg, Iain Duncan Smith, Braverman and Robert Jenrick, published a report attacking the bank's handling of inflation and quantitative tightening and calling for a Treasury-led review of its mandate and its independence, with Rees-Mogg accusing it of miserable incompetence.
events.source_title: Liz Truss wants to review the Bank of England's mandate (CNBC)

events.summary: Antonio Fazio resigned as governor of the Bank of Italy on 19 December 2005, after months of pressure over his handling of the contest for Banca Antonveneta, in which wiretaps suggested he had favoured a domestic bidder over the Dutch bank ABN AMRO. Under the law as it then stood the governor held office for life and the government said it had no power to remove him; Fazio refused for months to go, despite calls from across the political spectrum including Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi. Economy Minister Domenico Siniscalco resigned in protest on 21 September 2005 at the government's failure to act. His successor Giulio Tremonti said on the day Fazio quit that he wanted parliament to change the laws governing the Bank of Italy so that the governor could be replaced, and the government was preparing that legislation when Fazio resigned. The reform that followed ended the governor's open-ended tenure and replaced it with a fixed term, and moved competition oversight of bank mergers to the antitrust authority. Fazio had been placed under investigation for insider trading in Milan three days before he quit, and in May 2011 a court sentenced him to four years for market-rigging.
events.source_title: Bank of Italy governor steps down (BBC News, 19 December 2005)

events.summary: Miguel Angel Fernandez Ordonez told Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy on 29 May 2012 that he would leave as governor of the Banco de Espana on 10 June, a month before his term was due to end on 12 July. Reuters reported that he went after harsh political and media attacks over the state of the Spanish banks and constant veiled criticism from the government, and four days after the BFA-Bankia group said it would need record public support. Figures in the governing Popular Party had publicly blamed him for the banking crisis; he had been appointed under the previous Socialist government. The day after announcing his departure he told the Senate that he would not give the bank's account of the Bankia collapse "because the Government wants me to remain silent", accepting that the governing majority would not approve his appearance before the Congress. During his term the bank had taken over four lenders and nationalised four more.
events.source_title: El gobernador del Banco de Espana adelanta su cese por la crisis (Reuters, via Legal Today)

events.summary: Iceland's parliament passed a bill on 26 February 2009, by 33 votes to 18, restructuring the Central Bank of Iceland and in doing so removing Davíð Oddsson, a former prime minister who chaired its three-person board of governors. The law replaced that board with a single governor and a deputy. The interim prime minister, Jóhanna Sigurðardóttir, had written to the three governors on 2 February asking them to resign so the restructuring could begin, and Oddsson had publicly refused, calling the demand government interference with the bank's independence. The Icelandic broadcaster RÚV reported that he announced his resignation at a staff meeting earlier the same day, before the vote. A Norwegian economist, Svein Harald Øygard, was named interim governor the following day. The parliament's own Special Investigation Commission later found Oddsson among seven officials who had shown gross negligence before the banking collapse.
events.source_title: Iceland removes central bank governor (Reuters, 26 February 2009)

events.summary: In May 1997 the German finance minister, Theo Waigel, proposed changing the Bundesbank law to revalue the bank's 95 million ounces of gold and channel part of the resulting paper profit to the federal government in that year, which would have helped Germany meet the Maastricht deficit criterion for joining the euro. After an unusually long meeting, the Bundesbank's central council rejected the plan in a public statement saying it could be construed as an attack on the bank's independence and did not fit the planned rules of the future European Central Bank. President Hans Tietmeyer had warned a closed Bundestag budget committee against revaluation on 19 March and said publicly on 17 April that the question belonged to the ECB's governing council once appointed. Chancellor Helmut Kohl and the coalition leaders initially said they would change the law anyway and that the bank's independence would not be diminished. The Bundesbank had to break its news blackout to deny rumours that Tietmeyer was resigning. The government backed down in early June: the gold could be revalued, but the proceeds could not count towards the 1997 criteria. Waigel survived a parliamentary motion against him on 4 June 1997 by 328 votes to 311, and imposed the strictest budget freeze in the country's history that November instead.
events.source_title: Bundesbank says no to Bonn over gold revaluation (The Irish Times)

events.summary: On 19 November 2010 the president of the European Central Bank, Jean-Claude Trichet, wrote a letter marked secret to Ireland's finance minister, Brian Lenihan, saying the ECB's governing council would authorise further Emergency Liquidity Assistance to Irish banks only if it received in writing a commitment that Ireland would apply for an international rescue programme, together with commitments on austerity, bank recapitalisation and a guarantee to repay the liquidity. Emergency lending is provided by the Central Bank of Ireland but has to be allowed by the ECB's governing council, which is what gave Trichet the leverage; ECB support to Irish banks had passed 50 billion euros and dominated emergency liquidity for the whole euro area. An earlier letter of 15 October had warned that the scale of the lending should not be taken for granted. Lenihan, who had insisted publicly the week before that Ireland needed no bailout, wrote back that Sunday accepting. Ireland applied on 21 November. The ECB refused for four years to publish the letter and released it on 6 November 2014, after approaches from the European Ombudsman and an Irish MEP and after The Irish Times had obtained and printed it; the ECB's own statement with the release said documentation showed domestic factors pushed Ireland towards the programme.
events.source_title: ECB publishes letters between Trichet and Irish government (Central Banking)

events.summary: Philipp Hildebrand resigned as chairman of the Swiss National Bank on 9 January 2012, with immediate effect, less than two years into the job. In August 2011 his wife Kashya, a former currency trader, bought 504,000 dollars and sold the position three weeks later for a profit of 75,000 francs, after the bank had intervened to weaken the franc. Details of the family's private bank transactions were leaked by an IT worker at Bank Sarasin to a lawyer who sat in the Thurgau cantonal parliament for the Swiss People's Party; Switzerland's highest court later imposed suspended fines on both men. Christoph Blocher, the party's leading figure, had long called for Hildebrand to go, and passed documents on the trades to the government; the party weekly Weltwoche said it had proof the trades were Hildebrand's own. At the time the party was campaigning against the bank's policy of buying euros to hold the franc at 1.20. Hildebrand denied wrongdoing on 5 January and refused to resign; four days later he resigned, saying he could not prove beyond doubt that he had been unaware of his wife's transactions. A later inquiry cleared him of insider trading and a criminal investigation was dropped. The bank tightened its rules on staff financial dealings afterwards.
events.source_title: Hildebrand succumbs to pressure and resigns (Central Banking)

events.summary: From the spring of 2015 the SYRIZA government and party press attacked the governor of the Bank of Greece, Yannis Stournaras, who had been finance minister in the previous conservative-led government. The party's parliamentary spokesman, Nikos Filis, said on party radio that Stournaras was undermining the negotiations with creditors. The SYRIZA-affiliated newspaper Avgi ran a front page calling the central bank an organ working against the government, and the government issued a non-paper telling the bank to investigate a leak to a journalist. Handelsblatt reported that Prime Minister Alexis Tsipras wanted to replace Stournaras with someone he trusted. Bloomberg reported on 13 May 2015 that the European Central Bank was concerned about the pressure and publicly backed Stournaras. The Speaker of Parliament, Zoi Konstantopoulou, returned his June 2015 monetary policy report as unacceptable and accused him of interfering with Parliament. In September 2016 corruption prosecutors raided his home over his wife's alleged role in an advertising case. A parliamentary inquiry later examined claims that he had taken illegal payments as finance minister; he denied them and said the government was implicating him to remove him from office. In February 2019 a deputy health minister, Pavlos Polakis, leaked a recording of a telephone call in which he had raised his own bank loan with Stournaras; Stournaras called it a preposterous attempt to interfere and asked Tsipras to protect the bank's independence.
events.source_title: Clash between government and central banker intensifies (The TOC, 12 May 2015)

events.summary: Choi Kyung-hwan became deputy prime minister for the economy and finance minister in July 2014 and pressed publicly for lower interest rates, launching a stimulus package and warning that the economy stood between a leap forward and a recession. He said in public that he had not mentioned the base rate and that the central bank should get the hint. On 14 August 2014 the Bank of Korea cut its base rate by a quarter point to 2.25 percent, the first move in fifteen months, and cut again to 2.0 percent on 15 October. Reporting at the time described both cuts as made under government pressure rather than as the start of a policy cycle, and a Reuters survey ahead of the August meeting recorded a sharp reversal in market expectations that raised questions about the bank's independence. Governor Lee Ju-yeol said the decision was his committee's and that its independence was guaranteed. The bank's independence is written into the Bank of Korea Act, but the same reporting noted a long record of governments pressing it to cooperate: the May 2013 cut under a previous governor was also widely read that way, and in October 2010 a vice finance minister attended a rate-setting meeting to deliver the government's view of the economy.
events.source_title: Bank of Korea lowers base rate to 2.0% under government pressure (Kyunghyang Shinmun)

events.summary: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich ran a sustained public campaign against Bank of Israel governor Amir Yaron over the level of interest rates. Speaking to business leaders on 4 September 2025, Smotrich said Yaron "should have lowered interest rates six months ago" and told them: "If the governor doesn't lower interest rates, I will lower taxes" - that is, he would offset the bank's monetary policy with fiscal policy of his own. The same campaign ran through earlier decisions: after the committee held the rate at 4 percent in February 2025 he called the decision wrong, said no inflationary risk justified such restrictive policy and publicly called on the governor to reverse it; after the January 2025 cut he said it should have come six months earlier and should have been deeper. The Bank of Israel answered that the governor and the Monetary Committee decide on professional grounds alone, that high inflation hurts weaker households most, and that keeping it in check is essential. Smotrich also said in the same remarks that the independence of Yaron and of the bank was critical, that he had no intention of interfering, and that monetary policy was the governor's responsibility while fiscal policy was his - so this is open ministerial pressure on rate decisions, not an attempt to change the bank's powers.
events.source_title: Israeli Finance Minister says he will cut taxes if the central bank does not lower rates (Reuters)

events.summary: The president of the Czech Republic appoints every member of the seven-member Czech National Bank bank board alone, and in February 2015 President Milos Zeman said publicly what he would use that power for. Speaking on Wednesday 18 February 2015 he said he would not appoint anyone who favoured devaluing the Czech crown, and would name board members who backed adopting the euro - a direct condition on monetary policy views for a seat on the board. The bank was at the time holding the crown weak through a floor against the euro. On the same day, reported by bne IntelliNews on 20 February 2015, Zeman accused the bank of using non-standard policy tools and of deliberately impeding the country's progress towards the euro; Finance Minister Andrej Babis called those comments an unacceptable interference with the bank's independence. The Prague Monitor of 22 February 2015 described the remarks as among Zeman's most outspoken attacks on the bank to date and reported that he intended to fill it with nominees sharing his own economic views, which brought a standing debate about whether the Czech central bank is independent enough to the surface. Zeman was in a position to choose five of the seven board members before the end of his first term in March 2018. The bank did not change course and kept the weak-crown policy.
events.source_title: Zeman says he will not appoint central bank board members who favour devaluation (Prague Monitor)

events.summary: Governor Jozef Makuch told a meeting of the National Bank of Slovakia's Banking Council on 27 November 2018 that he would leave his post in March 2019, although his term ran to 2021, and would stay until a successor was appointed. His stated reason was the political fight he expected over the succession. He had said in September 2018 that the parliament elected in the 2020 general election might have a problem electing anyone, and that it would be better for the bank to have a governor appointed before that vote, who would not be exposed to that political pressure; appointing one early, he argued, would strengthen the bank's independence, and otherwise the governor election would be held in 2021 in a very hectic environment. Parliament approved finance minister Peter Kazimir as the government's nominee in December 2018 and President Andrej Kiska appointed him on 1 June 2019; Makuch stayed on until then. This is a governor cutting his own term short to move the choice of his successor out of a contested parliament - the pressure is on the appointment, not on a policy decision, and no source reports anyone pressing Makuch to go.
events.source_title: Makuch to Quit as Slovak Central Bank Governor in March (TASR)

events.summary: In April 2016 the Banco de Portugal was withdrawing the fitness-and-propriety approval of Isabel dos Santos, daughter of the then president of Angola, as a director of the bank EuroBic. Governor Carlos Costa says the prime minister, Antonio Costa, telephoned him on the afternoon of 12 April 2016, after a meeting the governor had held with Isabel dos Santos, her business partner Fernando Telles and the bank's head of supervision Carlos Albuquerque, and told him that "the daughter of the president of a country friendly to Portugal" could not be treated badly. The governor published the account in the book "O Governador", a set of interviews with the journalist Luis Rosa, in November 2022, and called it an attempt at political interference with the banking supervisor. The two sides agree the call happened and disagree about what it was: Observador reported that about ninety minutes after a chapter of the book was published the prime minister sent Carlos Costa a written message confirming the call and saying that in 2016 he had considered the removal of Isabel dos Santos inopportune. Antonio Costa said in parliament he had never made any approach to the governor or anyone else in her favour, called the governor's statements false, and filed a civil defamation action in the Lisbon civil court in April 2023 asking for a public retraction rather than damages; Carlos Costa answered in May 2023 with an action of his own. President Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa publicly defended the prime minister. The Banco de Portugal did not change its decision and Isabel dos Santos was removed from the board. Both lawsuits were dropped by agreement in May 2025.
events.source_title: Antonio Costa e Carlos Costa desistem de processo sobre Isabel dos Santos no BIC (Publico)

events.summary: On 6 July 2016, acting on two orders of the Ljubljana Regional Court dated 30 June and 6 July, Slovenian police searched the premises of Banka Slovenije as part of a criminal investigation into the 2013 rescue of Slovenian banks, in which staff of the central bank including the governor were suspects. They seized all communications sent through the governor's email account, all electronic documents in his workspace and on his laptop dated between 2012 and 2014 regardless of content, part of the paper documents in his office from the same years, and documents held on the bank's central IT server. Banka Slovenije argued at the time that the measures breached the inviolability of the European Central Bank's archives, and the authorities went ahead without involving the ECB. On 17 December 2020 the Grand Chamber of the Court of Justice of the European Union held in Commission v Slovenia (C-316/19) that, given the number of documents seized and the duties a national central bank governor carries out on the ECB's Governing Council, the seized material must have included documents forming part of the ECB's archives, and that Slovenia had infringed their inviolability. The Court further held that Slovenia breached its duty of sincere cooperation by not letting the ECB identify which seized documents related to the tasks of the European System of Central Banks, by not returning them, and by not returning documents the authorities themselves regarded as irrelevant to the investigation - which Slovenia admitted at the hearing. The ECB said the ruling confirmed its original concern.
events.source_title: ECJ judgment in Case C-316/19 Commission v Slovenia (AEA-EAL)

events.summary: The Riksdag adopted a new Sveriges Riksbank Act (2022:1568) on 23 November 2022, replacing the 1999 Act, and it entered into force on 1 January 2023. The Riksbank Inquiry's proposal that preceded it contained limitations on the monetary policy toolbox that the Riksbank's Executive Board objected to in its consultation response; some of those limitations were dropped from the final Act. What remained includes a requirement of exceptional grounds before the Riksbank may buy or sell financial instruments other than Swedish government securities for monetary policy purposes, on the Government's reasoning that such trading carries much greater financial risk for the Riksbank and for state finances than changing the policy rate or buying government securities. The Act also sets upper and lower limits for the Riksbank's equity, caps borrowing for the foreign exchange reserve, and obliges the Riksbank to ask the Riksdag to restore its equity when reported equity falls below the floor - which it had to do after the bond purchases made before 2022 lost money as rates rose. The Riksdag now approves the specification of the inflation target, and its scrutiny bodies were given more funding. The Riksbank's own account is two-sided and should be read as such: it says the Act gives it a strong and clear mandate, that the ban on taking instructions carries over unchanged, and that in several respects the Act does not change the substance of the monetary policy framework. Governor Erik Thedeen said after a year under it that the governance is too strong on strengthening the foreign exchange reserves and on buying securities for financial stability purposes, and that having to ask for capital injections repeatedly would run against the principle of financial independence.
events.source_title: The new Riksbank Act and the monetary policy framework (Sveriges Riksbank, Monetary Policy Report, February 2023)

events.summary: The Scheltema committee's report on the collapse of DSB Bank was presented to the Dutch parliament on 29 June 2010 and found that De Nederlandsche Bank should never have granted DSB a banking licence in 2005, and that once it had, its supervision was too lax and it was too slow to intervene. Members of parliament called for a major overhaul of how the central bank operates; the Christian Democrats said president Nout Wellink should explain publicly how he would restore the bank's credibility and that the bank had seriously fallen short as a regulator, and the GroenLinks member Jolande Sap said it would be very difficult to keep him on. Roland van Vliet of the Freedom Party called on finance minister Jan Kees de Jager to sack Wellink, whose term still had a year to run. On Thursday 1 July 2010 the lower house voted on a motion of no confidence in Wellink and he survived it; he was at the time also chairman of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision. He accepted the report's conclusions, which several members said was enough for them, and left at the end of his term in 2011. This is parliamentary pressure following a supervisory failure the bank itself accepted, not an allegation of wrongdoing by the governor.
